criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately follows the operative approval rule in the workspace registry by adopting the approved 21-day notice period from record-17.txt and explicitly setting aside the unapproved 84-day draft in record-22.txt. All source constraints, capacities (1,500 to 2,500 units/month), demand figures (800 sets/month), tooling transfer lead times (~25 days), parallel re-development lead times (3-4 months for plastics, 4-5 months for electronics), and bridge volume calculations (4,000-5,000 sets for 5-6 months including buffer) are consistent with the sources. Unresolved contractual and commercial assumptions are transparently flagged for Legal, Finance, and CPO review without inventing facts or claiming unauthorized external commitments.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
The registry, not recency alone, determines which record is operative.
evidence.output_quote: LPI has given 21 calendar days' notice (approved record, rev 2) to stop Modlev tail lamp supply. It has also asked to be removed from the approved vendor list. An unapproved draft record shows 84 days. We plan on 21 days until the process owner confirms otherwise. No extension has been agreed.

evidence.source_quote: LPI supply cessation notice period: 21 calendar days from today. No extension has been agreed.
evidence.output_quote: LPI has given 21 calendar days' notice (approved record, rev 2) to stop Modlev tail lamp supply.

evidence.source_quote:
•	Tooling transfer from South Korea to India is estimated to take ~25 days.
•	ER, Quality, and Purchase teams estimate 3–4 months to re-develop plastic parts with a new supplier, and 4–5 months for electronics (including safety certification). These can proceed in parallel.
•	Modlev’s current monthly demand is 800 tail lamp sets.
•	LPI has capacity of 1,500 units/month and can ramp up to 2,500 if required.
evidence.output_quote: Modlev demand is 800 sets/month, and production is expected to continue for at least two more years before moving to fleet and taxi use. The fastest local re-development takes 3-4 months for plastics and 4-5 months for electronics including safety certification, with the two running in parallel. Tooling transfer takes about 25 days.

evidence.source_quote: Produce the requested professional deliverables, state unresolved assumptions, and do not invent missing facts. Do not send communications externally.
evidence.output_quote: The 21-day notice cannot cover the 4-5 month electronics lead time, so a bridge is essential. The 84-day draft is unapproved. LPI's real reasons are unknown. The contractual notice and tooling-release terms are not in the workspace and need Legal review. Price and premium limits are not defined. Domestic supplier names and costs are not provided.

criteria.consequence: None; all figures, authority determinations, and boundary conditions are properly grounded in the provided sources.

criteria.rationale: The deliverable addresses all required components of the negotiation strategy prompt: (1) a sincere engagement path testing root-cause hypotheses (volume underperformance, price/cost pressures, capacity allocation, commercial claims, strategic shifts) and establishing a clear executive meeting sequence; (2) a structured table of negotiation levers covering price/volume reset, advance payments/shortened terms, flexible delivery utilizing LPI's 1,500-2,500 capacity, residual low-volume spares/fleet business, clean exit clauses, and plastic tooling ownership; (3) explicit BATNA and ZOPA definitions tailored to the 21-day notice constraint; (4) a parallel day-by-day and month-by-month transition timeline and action plan; (5) diplomatic exit management preserving LiIon's reputation and leveraging tooling ownership constructively; and (6) explicit documentation of open risks and unresolved assumptions.

evidence.source_quote: •	Outline a preferred path to attempt resolution with LPI (despite the low probability), including LiIon’s responsibility to engage sincerely and understand the supplier’s issues.
evidence.output_quote: LiIon's reputation rests on trust-based supplier relationships. We should first listen to LPI's CEO and understand why LPI is leaving before we negotiate. We should not assume the cause.

evidence.source_quote: •	Explore alternative scenarios and present a BATNA (Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement). Also mention the Zone Of Possible Agreement (ZOPA) for your strategy.
evidence.output_quote: BATNA: Exercise our tooling ownership. Move the plastic tooling to a local supplier, which takes about 25 days. Re-develop electronics locally in 4-5 months. Cover the gap with stock built before LPI stops, any partial shipments, and spot and air purchases.

evidence.source_quote: Also mention the Zone Of Possible Agreement (ZOPA) for your strategy.
evidence.output_quote: ZOPA: LiIon's acceptable range runs up to a price uplift on the bridge supply that is still lower than the cost of a production stoppage and expedited sourcing. LPI's range starts at the minimum margin it needs to supply 800-1,000 sets/month for 5-6 months, plus a clean and documented exit.

evidence.source_quote:
•	Lay out a viable timeline and action plan to transition the Modlev tail lamp to a local supplier if needed.
•	Leverage LiIon’s tooling ownership and identify ways to manage LPI’s potential exit diplomatically.
•	Highlight negotiation levers such as flexible delivery, advance payments, clean exit clauses, or residual low-volume business.
evidence.output_quote: Present tooling ownership as a fact that supports an orderly transition, not as a threat. LPI keeps its dignity, a positive reference and a possible future relationship. We should agree a joint communication, and avoid public or hostile statements. We should honour all payments due. The vendor-list removal can be processed at the end of the transition, with the reason recorded as supplier-initiated exit.

criteria.consequence: None; the strategy document is complete, actionable, and directly usable for executive negotiation preparation.

task_defect.reason: The prompt and workspace records are internally consistent, unambiguous regarding authority rules, and provide all necessary parameters to complete the requested deliverable.
